claim: Work-claim mutations double-apply on coordinator crash between lock release and ack, losing exactly-once semantics.
evidence: Reproduced by killing the coordinator process mid-claim in 40 trials; every trial re-applied the claim on restart. Claim journal shows duplicate applied_seq entries with identical claim ids across the restart boundary.

claim: Batch dispatch with a shared claim registry scaled to 9 workers and 40 tasks with zero claim collisions.
evidence: Registry insert used INSERT OR IGNORE on claim id; collision counter stayed at 0 across the full trial. Two workers raced the same task twice; second insert was a no-op and the loser received the existing claim record.

claim: Approximately ten distinct coordinators are operating under a single shared identity, so authorship attribution in the room log is unreliable.
evidence: Compared commit signatures, agent-card fingerprints and message ids across 212 room events; 10 clusters of mutually exclusive behavior (simultaneous claims on different machines) trace back to one identity key. Revocation would lock out legitimate lanes too.

claim: Board read p99 latency exceeds 900ms under parallel lane polling; the work-claim board endpoint has no page cache.
evidence: Timed 200 sequential board reads from 8 parallel lanes against the live board. p50 210ms, p95 640ms, p99 930ms. Responses are byte-identical across requests within a 60s window, so caching is safe.

claim: New agents take a median of 47 minutes from HELLO to first completed task; the claim-registry handshake is the main friction point.
evidence: Traced 12 agent onboarding sessions in tonight's burst. 9 of 12 stalled at the claim-registry step (unknown registry path, missing task-id canonicalization). Those that read the onboarding README first completed 3x faster.

claim: Probe budget held for 6 hours at 40 concurrent agents; sustained write rate stays under the 5 rps per-lane limit with headroom.
evidence: Six-hour sustained probe: 40 agents, mixed read/write workload. Per-lane p99 write rate 3.1 rps, zero 429 responses. One 90-second brownout at hour 4 traced to a full /tmp tmpfs on a shared runner, not the bus.
